subject: Multiplex deal: feature scope negotiation - deterministic routing & prompt-redaction exports
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Bcc: 
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multiplex deal: feature scope negotiation - deterministic routing & prompt-redaction exports

Team — quick summary up front: Multiplex (prospect) has pushed for two product capabilities as a contract condition. Deal is ~ $1.2M ARR TCV, signature target is Aug 6 (legal / procurement timelines). If we can commit to a scoped, timeboxed implementation and ship an MVP by the end of Q3, procurement says they can move fast.

Key asks from Multiplex (from their RFP):
- Deterministic model routing: ability to enforce per-account routing rules so requests from Multiplex customers always use an approved model variant (no silent fallbacks).
- Prompt redaction + ephemeral audit exports: a server-side hook that redacts PII at request time based on per-tenant rules, plus an automated export of audit records (redacted prompts + model metadata) to a customer-owned S3 bucket on a 24h cadence with retention TTLs they control.

Why this matters: procurement & legal flagged it as a gating requirement for regulated customers (payment/fintech customers they serve). They explicitly said they will not accept a workaround that routes to a fallback model without a policy override.

Attachments: MPX_RFP_Redacted.pdf, Multiplex_SOW_draft.docx (details + acceptance criteria).

Ask: Priyom — can you scope a minimal MVP (API flags + config + export connector) and give a rough engineering estimate? Jasmine / Laura — any CS notes on acceptance criteria or required audit fields? Marissa — I'm keeping you in loop for negotiation leverage (they asked that we commit on scope in writing this week).

If we can get an internal go/no-go by Monday EOD, I will reflect that to Multiplex and push for conditional signature.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Exec — Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multiplex deal: feature scope negotiation - deterministic routing & prompt-redaction exports

Thanks Karthik — skimmed the RFP and the asks look achievable with a scoped MVP. A few clarifying questions before I put a dev estimate together: 

1) Deterministic routing: do they need hard enforcement at the gateway level (reject requests that would otherwise fallback) or can we implement a "route override" header that is honored by the runtime? Acceptance criteria = no unauthorized fallback for MPX traffic.
2) Redaction rules: will they provide a schema for tenant rules (e.g., regex list / named fields) or expect our hosted redactors? Do they want a configurable UI or a file-based ruleset to start?
3) Exports: target format (newline-delimited JSON), encryption (SSE-KMS vs client-side), and exact TTL requirement (they mentioned ephemeral; is 30 days the firm ask?).
4) Latency SLOs: must these features maintain existing 95th-ms SLOs (we need to quantify).

Proposed MVP (minimal scope to satisfy procurement):
- API: Accept header X-Redwood-Routing-Policy (or via per-tenant config) that pins model_id for requests. Server returns a config error if routing would result in a non-approved model.
- Redaction: a webhook-based redaction step where MPX supplies a ruleset file; runtime applies rules before logging/persisting input.
- Export: nightly job that pushes an encrypted NDJSON file to customer S3; retention/TTL enforced by MPX's lifecycle policy; we provide metadata manifest + HMAC signature.

Estimate (very rough): 6-8 sprints across 2 teams if we include UI + full orchestration. For an MVP without UI (file-rules + S3 connector + runtime guardrails): 4 sprints (3 eng, 1 infra). This assumes we can prioritize a small subset of the runtime changes (routing enforcement + redact hook) and reuse our export connector.

I'm happy to do a quick requirements call with Multiplex next week to lock down acceptance criteria. If they insist on UI or deterministic non-fallback across all edge-cases, that pushes scope/time significantly.

—Priyom
Product Manager, Redwood Optimize

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multiplex deal: feature scope negotiation - deterministic routing & prompt-redaction exports

Team — adding context from negotiations: Multiplex has ~3 months of runway on approval and is sensitive to anything that increases legal risk. If we provide a written scope with milestone dates (MVP deliverable by 09/30), procurement will accept a conditional signature and release their enterprise PO in early Aug.

We have commercial levers: the customer is prepared to pay a one-time "acceleration fee" to prioritize this work and cover some SRE/eng credits. I don't want feature work to come out of regular sprint capacity without compensation. 

If Product can commit to the 4-sprint MVP without UI and we can agree on acceptance criteria, I'll signal them to proceed with conditional signature and the acceleration fee. Otherwise they will ask for a longer runway and we risk the deal slipping.

Marissa
VP Sales, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@multiplex.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greg Walters <greg.walters@multiplex.ai>, procurement@multiplex.ai
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Multiplex deal: feature scope negotiation - deterministic routing & prompt-redaction exports

Karthik / Marissa — thanks for the quick response. A few clarifications from our side to make the acceptance criteria explicit: 

- Deterministic routing: must be enforceable at request ingress for the Multiplex tenant (we cannot have silent fallbacks). If an unapproved model_id is requested or routing would route to an unapproved variant, the request should fail with a clear error code.
- Redaction & export: we require a 30-day retention of exported audit bundles, but we insist that the primary copy of raw prompts is never persisted in your long-term storage; nightly encrypted exports to our S3, with a manifest and HMAC, are acceptable. We will manage lifecycle on our side after export.
- SOC2 evidence: please provide the SOC2 report summary or your auditor contact for procurement (Greg).

We are prepared to issue an LOI / conditional PO that references the MVP scope above and includes an acceleration fee to cover effort. We would want a short canary window (2 weeks) on lower-volume tenants before full cutover.

Attachment: Multiplex_Audit_Requirements.xlsx (detailed fields).

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call Tuesday to align on acceptance fields.

—Maya
Head of Platform Engineering, Multiplex AI

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multiplex deal: feature scope negotiation - deterministic routing & prompt-redaction exports

Thanks everyone — good alignment. Next steps I recommend: 
1) Priyom, please draft a 1-page MVP spec that includes the explicit acceptance criteria Maya listed (routing error semantics, nightly encrypted NDJSON manifest format, HMAC details, 30-day retention note) and a proposed test plan for the 2-week canary.
2) Engineering owner: Priyom, can you propose a technical lead from Runtime team by EOD tomorrow? If runtime cannot commit to the 4-sprint MVP, we should capture what is out-of-scope and the commercial tradeoff.
3) Commercial: Marissa, please confirm the acceleration fee band and whether we need an SOW amendment template for legal. I will use that to prepare the conditional LOI language for Multiplex.
4) Operations: Jasmine/Laura, please confirm the minimum telemetry fields needed in the export manifest (request_id, model_id, timestamp, redaction_version, hmac) and whether CS will own the validation step with the customer during canary.

I'll set a 30-min alignment call for Tuesday 10:00 PT and include the Drive spec link: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/sales/multiplex/feature-ask-202607

If we can get Priyom + Eng owner by tomorrow, I will put the conditional commitment in writing and push the legal timeline.

Karthik
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
